**Section C: Reading Comprehension (10 marks).** Read the passage below carefully and answer the questions that follow using your own words as much as possible. The passage (adapted from "Educational reforms: the new slavery", *Change Magazine*) critically examines the educational system in Cameroon and Africa more broadly, arguing that it has long promised graduates power, wealth and status without preparing them for real-life realities, while noting recent government efforts to make education more practical and relevant.

1. What, according to the writer, is the fundamental problem with the educational system in Cameroon? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 1. **The educational system has, for decades, given graduates the false impression that they would automatically acquire power, high office, wealth and status** — a belief that has led to widespread frustration, since the system, copied largely from Western models, has neither made Cameroonians "Europeans" nor prepared them adequately for their own African realities.

The passage (adapted from "Educational reforms: the new slavery", *Change Magazine*) critically examines the educational system in Cameroon and Africa more broadly, arguing that it has long promised graduates power, wealth and status without preparing them for real-life realities, while noting recent government efforts to make education more practical and relevant.

2. With inspiration from the text, why do many of our children seek to go abroad? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 2. **After years of unemployment and frustration despite holding certificates and degrees, and faced with a chronic shortage of passport booklets reflecting a worsening local situation, many young people come to believe that conditions are better abroad**, imagining "clean streets" and easier opportunities than those available at home.

The passage (adapted from "Educational reforms: the new slavery", *Change Magazine*) critically examines the educational system in Cameroon and Africa more broadly, arguing that it has long promised graduates power, wealth and status without preparing them for real-life realities, while noting recent government efforts to make education more practical and relevant.

3. What does the writer insinuate when he says "...if the public service is closed then it would mean doom for our children"? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 3. **The writer suggests that many parents believe a government/public-service job is their child's only realistic path to success**, so much so that if that door were to close, they would see no other viable future for their children — reflecting an unhealthy overreliance on certificates and public employment rather than practical skills or entrepreneurship.

4. Give two differences between our Cameroonian children and Western children mentioned in the passage. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown: 4. **(1)** Cameroonian children, as described in the passage, often lack curiosity and stimulus to find out about their own country, replying that information "is not in the book" rather than seeking answers themselves. **(2)** They are less encouraged to express themselves freely, creatively and openly, unlike what the passage implies of children in more "relevant," practically-oriented educational systems.
